items.description: The Watcher prompt and campaign roadmap required Application Client consumer integration before future Watcher runtime launch, but the Watcher graph named only client-conformance.
items.rationale: The gate is a pre-product exact-revision attestation over completed public conformance evidence. It does not require Watcher runtime implementation, so client-conformance -> consumer-integration-gate -> watcher-runtime-core is acyclic. Retaining both external edges preserves explicit conformance and gate blocker truth.
items.terminalPath: Completed atomically when this disposition and watcher-runtime-core's external dependency on application-client/consumer-integration-gate land together in the combined client-conformance-shaping-152-v1 reconciliation packet.

evidence.details: The prompt says watcher-runtime-core remains planned until Application Client client-conformance and the consumer-integration gate permit it.
watcher-runtime-core depends on dumb-watcher-contract-gate and externally on Application Client client-conformance; it does not name consumer-integration-gate.

The roadmap keeps both consumer runtimes blocked through conformance and the consumer-integration gate, and keeps watcher-runtime-core planned until client-conformance proves the required cross-backend behavior.

Watcher, Application Client, and Operator Station authorities agreed that consumer-integration-gate is a pre-product exact-revision public-client consumability attestation after conformance. Watcher runtime implementation is not gate evidence.

Issue #152 owns one public-only cross-backend conformance bundle with Watcher-shaped send-only and Operator Station-shaped bidirectional probes. Both consumer authorities attest the same exact reviewed and green head before the gate is operated.

completionEvidence.gateBoundary: Public conformance evidence plus exact-revision consumer attestations; no Watcher runtime implementation.

items.description: Post-merge public-management validation at main d0237dbb found that Runtime::run plus LocalManagement::Remove fails with canonicalization-failed for an isolated unsupported v1 row whose opaque state is outside the v2 interoperable range, such as {"checksum":18446744073709551615}. The watch stays paused instead of being removed, because the management transaction computes v2 canonical state hashes for every admitted mutation.
items.rationale: Issue #162 cannot close while public removal of an isolated unsupported row fails. The design steward approved a bounded repair that preserves unsupported state losslessly, keeps the permanent ID and tombstone, explicitly audits when v2 state hashes do not apply, and leaves strict v2 canonicalization unchanged. PR #170 remains independently valid.
items.terminalPath: Completes when PR #173, which says Closes #162, passes required CI and review at its final head and Campaign merges it at the exact cleared SHA. Post-merge validation, the #162 field report, and final reconciliation follow under #162.

items.description: An exponent-form number such as 1e20 in an admitted detector request is re-encoded by JCS stdin encoding into an unsafe integral token that the parser rejects.
items.rationale: The repair is needed for #162's outcome. It separates transport serialization from JCS validation, hash, and evidence encoding, with no admission-policy change. Design steward session 4745cca8-006f-4422-9d35-cf056f28c31f approved it at 02:13 on 2026-10-23.

evidence.details: Owner finding: at runtime merge d0237dbb, parse_request accepts a request whose state holds 1e20, canonical_bytes rewrites it as 100000000000000000000, and parse_request then rejects those bytes with canonicalization-failed. The runtime uses this encoder for detector stdin. The steward approved an explicit ordinary-JSON request transport encoder in PR #173. Probe source and output are retained as request_roundtrip_probe.rs and post-merge-request-roundtrip-probe.log in the owner session artifacts.
The coordinator reported the steward approval and repair boundary at 02:13 on 2026-10-23.
